paragraphs: Greenzie makes self-driving software meant to improve the safety, productivity and profitability of a landscaping fleet. It partners with OEMs to manufacture Greenzie-equipped, Robotic Ready mowers sold at outdoor power equipment dealers throughout the United States. Buyers shop for those mowers at dealer locations nationwide.

Each Greenzie-equipped mower carries sensors the company says are field tested for obstacle avoidance, smooth driving and clean stripes. Operators can switch between manual and autonomous modes. A crew mows the perimeter once and lets the software finish the job while they move on to other tasks. The software is designed in accordance with ANSI/RIA R15.08-1-2020 safety requirements for industrial robots.

The customers are commercial landscaping crews, and the company frames its work as making jobs easier, faster and safer for large landscapers across the country. Greenzie began in 2018, when co-founder Charles Brian Quinn started calling every landscaper he could reach. The team describes itself as roboticists, software engineers and landscaping professionals. It says it is backed by venture capital firms and investors.

quote.text: Our big mission is to free humans from repetitive outdoor labor.
